events.title: Target approach
events.description: Approach preparation ahead of arrival on day 275 (time of flight); science starts on day 290.

events.title: Uncertain target illumination
events.description: Approach imaging shows the target is darker than the pre-launch scenario estimate, so each observation collects less usable signal per hour. Why this happened: the event set neo-default-v1 declares this scenario event in the approach window (days 245-290); its day is drawn from the seeded scenario stream. Extend the observations or keep the planned schedule? Options: Keep the planned schedule (keep-schedule): No extra data volume or propellant; measurements keep their planned observation time.; Extend the observations (extend-observation): Observations run at 1.5x their duty cycle (more scheduled time and collected data), but the buffer fills faster and the extra attitude work uses 3 % of the propellant.. Chosen: Extend the observations (player choice). Its day is a seeded scenario uncertainty; the effects are deterministic.

choices.label: Keep the planned schedule
choices.tradeoff: No extra data volume or propellant; measurements keep their planned observation time.

choices.label: Extend the observations
choices.tradeoff: Observations run at 1.5x their duty cycle (more scheduled time and collected data), but the buffer fills faster and the extra attitude work uses 3 % of the propellant.

events.title: Arrival maneuver

events.title: Observation: meas-shape-model
events.description: Observation of meas-shape-model for 4 h at duty cycle 0.0225; data is stored in the onboard buffer until the next contact. The planned duty cycle was changed by event scenario-target-illumination.

events.title: Missed contact: data backlog
events.description: The ground station loses lock during a pass and the planned contact is missed; with no slack in the downlink plan the collected data stays on board and a data backlog builds up. Why this happened: the analysis flags the downlink (data-return warning): with comms-xband-medium the worst link margin is +6.71 dB and the contact plan has no slack, so a lost pass turns into a backlog. How should operations respond to the fading link? Options: Halve the downlink rate (lower-rate): About 3 dB more link margin for the rest of the mission, but each pass returns half the data, so the backlog drains slowly.; Keep the planned rate (keep-rate): Full-rate passes once the link recovers, but the marginal link keeps dropping passes for the next 6 days and the backlog grows.. Chosen: Keep the planned rate (player choice). The effects follow a deterministic design rule.

events.title: Solar particle event: safe-mode prompt
events.description: A solar particle event raises the radiation dose and the risk of memory upsets in the onboard buffer. Why this happened: the event set neo-default-v1 declares this scenario event in the science-ops window (days 290-320); its day is drawn from the seeded scenario stream. Enter safe mode or keep the science timeline running? Options: Enter safe mode (pause science) (pause-science): No risk to the spacecraft or its data, but observations in the next 10 days are not flown.; Continue science (continue): No science time lost, but upsets corrupt half of the buffered data and the heaters drain 25 % of the battery.. Chosen: Continue science (player choice). Its day is a seeded scenario uncertainty; the effects are deterministic.

finalReport.summary: Flown run of a marginal design: 0/2 objectives achieved; 42% of the science returned, 83% collected; score 85.5. 3 anomaly/scenario event(s) occurred.

dimensions.explanation: Returned-data science coverage is 68 of 100 (collected data that is not downlinked does not count).
10 of 10 hard gates pass (design-time proxy; refined by simulation).
Mean of 4 mass, delta-v, energy and data headrooms relative to the required headroom (full credit at the hard-gate threshold, zero at no headroom).
Cost $58,678,522 is within the $60,000,000 budget; spending less is not rewarded on its own.

realizedRisks: target-illumination (decision, day 258.848): Uncertain target illumination; choice: Extend the observations
missed-contact (anomaly, day 291): Missed contact: data backlog; choice: Keep the planned rate
solar-event (decision, day 302.668): Solar particle event: safe-mode prompt; choice: Continue science
rootCauses: Downlink capacity 1.07e+10 bit is below the 1.56e+10 bit needed (generated 1.3e+10 bit plus 20% margin); only 1.07e+10 of 1.3e+10 bit is downlinked, so collected science is not fully returned.
Uncertain target illumination (day 258.848): the event set neo-default-v1 declares this scenario event in the approach window (days 245-290); its day is drawn from the seeded scenario stream.

Missed contact: data backlog (day 291): the analysis flags the downlink (data-return warning): with comms-xband-medium the worst link margin is +6.71 dB and the contact plan has no slack, so a lost pass turns into a backlog.

Solar particle event: safe-mode prompt (day 302.668): the event set neo-default-v1 declares this scenario event in the science-ops window (days 290-320); its day is drawn from the seeded scenario stream.
counterfactuals: Upgrade communications (e.g. higher-gain antenna) or reduce observation duty cycle: Raises downlink capacity or lowers generated data so more science is returned.
Reduce observation duty cycle: Generates less data.
Plan more or longer downlink contacts: Adds capacity.
Plan observation time with margin over each requirement so an illumination surprise does not leave a measurement short.

Give the downlink plan slack (more or longer contacts, a higher-gain radio or a lower planned data volume) so the analysis data-return and link-margin checks pass and one lost pass does not leave data on board.
Schedule observations with slack so a safe-mode pause does not remove a required measurement, and downlink often so little data is exposed in the buffer.
limitations: deterministic event simulation; not orbital propagation
Launch/deployment lasts 1 d and commissioning 14 d (gameplay defaults, capped to 5 % / 25 % of the time of flight, or of the time before science when there is no transfer).
Approach starts 30 d before arrival (at most half the transfer); mid-course starts halfway through the cruise (gameplay defaults).
Without an interplanetary transfer, cruise (orbit raising / checkout) and mid-course (orbit trim) each last 1 d (gameplay durations).
Science operations span the observation plan; downlink-return runs to the end of the mission.
Telemetry is sampled at phase, maneuver, observation and contact checkpoints from the engineering analysis; it is not a time-stepped subsystem simulation.
Battery state of charge is the end-of-cycle value of the analysis representative power cycle for the phase; the battery is full at launch (gameplay-estimate).
Pointing error is a proxy equal to the ADCS pointing accuracy (gameplay-estimate).
Link margin is reported at contacts only, at the scenario reference Earth range.
Design anomalies fire only where the engineering analysis flags the matching constraint; the only randomness is the day of each declared scenario event, drawn from its own seeded scenario stream.

Event effects are gameplay-estimate approximations: skipped observations and missed contacts are re-analysed by the engine; lost buffer data can no longer be downlinked (downlinked = min(downlinked, generated - lost)); battery dips recover by the next checkpoint.
Plan items are skipped, missed, rescaled or cancelled whole by their start day; an item that starts before an effect window and runs into it is flown in full (approximation).
Propellant effects are telemetry-only: they move the propellant channel (clamped at 0) but do not change the maneuver budget.
All catalogue values are illustrative gameplay-estimate archetypes.
